claims.statement: All 186 held orders fall within scope EXC-0921 (rule v18 split-reservation orders routed to east node)
claims.limitation: Perfectly correlated but cannot yet separate rule-change effect from east-node-lane infrastructure effect

claims.statement: No held orders exist outside the EXC-0921 scope (no other node or allocation pattern is affected)
claims.limitation: Strengthens evidence of rule v18 involvement but does not prove rule defect vs. carrier issue

claims.statement: Stale 2023 runbook suggests rolling back allocation rule sets after allocation changes cause held orders
claims.limitation: 2023 document, procedures may have changed; suggests a pattern of allocation rules causing hold-ups

claims.statement: Rule set v18's split-reservation logic creates orders that the east-node lanes cannot fulfill (either because the rule reserves stock incorrectly or because the split structure is incompatible with the carrier pickup model)
claims.limitation: Requires examination of rule v18 design and test coverage to confirm

claims.statement: The east-node carrier or scheduling system has a capacity or integration issue specific to split-reservation orders from rule v18
claims.limitation: Observability gap prevents direct inspection of carrier-side state

next_action.rationale: Rule v18 is the sole differentiator for all 186 held orders. Reviewing its design change, test results, and any known issues in its deployment history will determine whether the split-reservation logic has a documented defect or works as designed. This discriminates between a rule implementation problem (which suggests rollback or correction) and a carrier/scheduling problem (which suggests integration diagnostic or east-node investigation).
